reason: Paper will be needed for printing, so I'll start with plant fiber and water.
expectation: I expect this to produce paper or a pulp for making it, though I'm not certain.

alternatives.reason: Charcoal and water may make ink, but I'll start with the paper.
Carving the planks may help build the press, but paper seems a useful first step.

effect: The fiber and water made pulp, so I can continue toward paper.
reason: Cloth may help form or dry the pulp into paper.
expectation: I expect paper, or an intermediate sheet that still needs drying.

alternatives.reason: Ink is also needed, but I'll finish the paper first.

effect: The pulp and cloth produced paper, so I can move on to ink or the press.
reaction: Making paper from pulp was straightforward.
reason: Charcoal and water seem like a practical way to make the ink mentioned in the chapter.
expectation: I expect to make ink, possibly with another preparation step.

alternatives.reason: Carving planks may make a press component, but I want to prepare ink first.

effect: Charcoal and water made ink, leaving the press to build.
reaction: The ink came together as expected.
reason: Carving planks may produce a printing block or another press component.
expectation: I expect a carved wooden component for printing, though its exact role is unclear.

alternatives.reason: Planks and iron may make the press frame, but I'll try carving first.

effect: Carving the planks made a printing block, which can now be inked.
reaction: The carved block makes sense as a way to reproduce an image or text.
reason: I'll ink the block to prepare it for printing.
expectation: I expect an inked printing block, ready to transfer a print onto paper.

alternatives.reason: Planks and iron might form the press frame, but I'll prepare the block first.

effect: The printing block is inked and ready for a later printing step.
reason: Planks and iron seem useful for building the press itself.
expectation: I expect a press frame or another structural component, though its exact form is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Paper and planks might also contribute to printing, but the press structure seems more pressing.

effect: The press is built, and the new goal is to print a page using the prepared materials.
reaction: The screw and plate explanation makes the press's operation clear.
reason: I'll place the inked block at the press to prepare for printing.
expectation: I expect the block to be placed at the press so paper can be pressed against it.

alternatives.reason: Placing the paper first may also work, but the block seems a natural starting point.

effect: The inked block is in place, so paper can now be used at the press.
reason: Combining the paper with the inked block at the press directly addresses the goal.

effect: The press produced printed pages and completed the final goal.
reaction: Seeing the same marks reproduced ties the materials and press together satisfyingly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the press was most worthwhile: the screw-and-plate explanation made its operation clear, and it opened the printing goal.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inking the block felt straightforward but less interesting than building and using the press.

surprise.text: The press was created directly from planks and iron; I had expected a frame or intermediate component.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary, though the role of cloth in making paper was not explained.

continue.text: I would continue: assembling the press and seeing the finished pages made the chain of materials feel purposeful.
